column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “he made,” without naming the maker here; BSB supplies “Bezalel.”
The Hebrew changes from plural “they hammered” to singular “he cut”; BSB uses “they” for both actions. The Hebrew also repeats “in among” for the four materials.
The Hebrew calls the joining points “its two ends”; BSB calls them “its two corners.”

The Hebrew makes the breastpiece the object of “they bound,” with its rings connecting it to the ephod’s rings; BSB makes the rings themselves the object of “they tied.”
The Hebrew says “he made” the robe; BSB says “they made” it.
The Hebrew describes the opening as a “mouth” and its edging as a “lip”; BSB uses “opening” and “collar.”
The Hebrew lists blue, purple, and scarlet, followed by “twisted”; it does not explicitly name linen here. BSB adds “and finely spun linen.”
The Hebrew repeats “between the pomegranates” twice; BSB expresses the placement once.
The Hebrew repeats “a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate”; BSB condenses this to “alternating bells and pomegranates.”
